title: Words of Warmth: Trust and Sociability Norms for over 26k English Words

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating co-occurring Warmth, Competence, Trust, and Sociability (WCTS) scores for religious target terms (e.g., 'muslim', 'jew') in a large corpus of social media posts.
Analyzing co-term WCTS scores for target terms (e.g., 'immigrant', 'america', 'canada') in geo-located tweets to examine ingroup/outgroup behavior and national stereotypes.
Plotting co-term Warmth and Competence scores for age-related terms (e.g., 'elderly') to measure placement on the Stereotype Content Model space.
Evaluating co-term Warmth and Competence scores for body-size related terms (e.g., 'underweight', 'overweight', 'obese') in social media text.
Comparing direct Trust vs. Sociability scores and utilizing co-term Warmth and Competence analysis for terms like 'homosexual' and 'lgbtq'.
Comparing direct lexicon scores and co-occurring WCTS scores for gendered terms (e.g., 'father', 'mother', 'husband', 'wife') to identify traditional warmth vs. competence gender stereotypes.
Mapping various professions (e.g., 'nurse', 'doctor', 'teacher', 'CEO') on the Warmth-Competence quadrant space using direct lexicon lookup and social media co-term analysis.
